What factor of a wetland affects migratory birds? and if the factor changes in the future, how will behaviour change?

```{r load package, message=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel)
library(readr)
library(readxl)
library(lubridate)
```

=============================================================
GPS clean-up
=============================================================
All times from here on are UTC. Each raw GPS file is read in the clock it was written in:
GrusVipio_GPS.csv (br22063, br22064, br23011, br23018) is in Korean local time (KST, no daylight saving);
the Movebank file for 27233947 (White_naped_crane_Mongolia_WSCC) is in UTC.
```{r}
gps_clock_tz <- "Asia/Seoul"   # GrusVipio_GPS.csv. Set "UTC" when this script is run on the WSCC/Movebank file.

crane_data <- read.csv("/Users/yjkang/Desktop/NIE_BigData/Grus_Vipio/GrusVipio_GPS.csv", check.names = FALSE)
crane_data$timestamp_clean <- with_tz(as.POSIXct(crane_data$Datetime, format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S",
                                                 tz = gps_clock_tz), "UTC")
crane_data

# Drop missing coordinates and keep points where HDOP is <= 5 
# (we also keep NAs just in case the logger dropped the HDOP value but kept a valid 3D fix)
clean_hdop <- subset(crane_data, !is.na(`latitude`) & !is.na(`longitude`))
clean_hdop <- subset(clean_hdop, `GPS_DOP` <= 5 | is.na(`GPS_DOP`))
clean_hdop
```

```{r}
library(argosfilter)
speed_threshold_ms <- 80 * (1000 / 3600) #biological speed threshold (80 km/h converted to m/s)

# split the dataframe by individual, sort by time, apply the mask, and recombine.
clean_pkg_list <- lapply(split(clean_hdop, clean_hdop$`ID`), function(bird_data) {
  
  # Sort chronologically
  bird_data <- bird_data[order(bird_data$timestamp_clean), ]
  bird_data <- bird_data[!duplicated(bird_data$timestamp_clean), ]
  # Run the argosfilter velocity mask
  filter_flags <- vmask(lat = bird_data$`latitude`, 
                        lon = bird_data$`longitude`, 
                        dtime = bird_data$timestamp_clean, 
                        vmax = speed_threshold_ms)
  return(bird_data[filter_flags %in% c("not", "end_location"), ])
})

final_clean_data <- do.call(rbind, clean_pkg_list)
print(paste("Original points:", nrow(crane_data)))
print(paste("Cleaned points:", nrow(final_clean_data)))
final_clean_data

#repeat for White_naped_crane_Mongolia_WSCC.csv
#write.csv(final_clean_data, "/Users/yjkang/Desktop/NIE_BigData/wetland_birds/data/birdGPStrajectory/cleaned_White_naped_crane_Mongolia_WSCC.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

=============================================================
GPS to continuous time-series
=============================================================
```{r}
#convert lat/lon to UTM (meters), mathematically flatten the map using a projection.
#For Mongolia/China (around Longitude 110°E), UTM Zone 49N is the standard projection.
library(sf)
# 1. Convert Long/Lat to a spatial object (WGS84 = EPSG 4326)
hmm_sf <- st_as_sf(final_clean_data, 
                   coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), 
                   crs = 4326) 

# 2. Project the coordinates to meters (UTM Zone 49N = EPSG 32649)
hmm_sf_proj <- st_transform(hmm_sf, crs = 32649)
coords_proj <- st_coordinates(hmm_sf_proj) # Extract the new metric coordinates back out

# Format the data for momentuHMM. columns specifically named "ID", "time", "x", "y"
hmm_data <- data.frame(
  ID = final_clean_data$`ID`,
  time = final_clean_data$timestamp_clean,
  x = coords_proj[, "X"], # Now in exact meters!
  y = coords_proj[, "Y"]  # Now in exact meters!
)
hmm_data <- hmm_data[hmm_data$ID %in% c("br22063", "br22064", "br23018", "br23011"), ] #eastMongolian population
hmm_data <- hmm_data[order(hmm_data$ID, hmm_data$time), ] #Ensure data is strictly ordered by ID and Time.
hmm_data
```

#Test if there are problematic data gaps, etc.
```{r, fig.height=4, fig.width=3}
bad_bird <- hmm_data[hmm_data$ID == "br23011", ]

print(nrow(bad_bird)) #Count total rows (Is it too sparse? < 50 points?)
print(sum(duplicated(bad_bird$time)))  #Look for duplicate timestamps. if this number is > 0, crawlWrap will automatically fail.
time_diffs <- diff(bad_bird$time)
print(max(time_diffs)) # Are there gaps of weeks/months?
```

```{r}
#dealing with massive time gaps
gap_threshold <-24 * 60  # 7 days = 7 * 24 * 60 = 10080 minutes

# split tracks with massive gaps
hmm_data_fixed <- hmm_data %>%
  group_by(ID) %>%
  arrange(time, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    time_diff = as.numeric(difftime(time, lag(time), units = "mins")),
    # The first point has no previous point, so set to 0
    time_diff = ifelse(is.na(time_diff), 0, time_diff),
    # Flag any step that jumps by more than threshold (1) or not (0)
    gap_flag = ifelse(time_diff > gap_threshold, 1, 0),
    # Create a cumulative sum for the burst.  Example: 0, 0, 0, (gap!), 1, 1, 1, (gap!), 2, 2...
    burst_num = cumsum(gap_flag) + 1,
    # Create a temporary new ID column to avoid grouping conflicts
    temp_ID = paste0(ID, "_", burst_num)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # Safely overwrite the main ID column AFTER ungrouping
  mutate(ID = temp_ID) %>%
  # Drop the temporary columns to keep things clean
  select(-time_diff, -gap_flag, -burst_num, -temp_ID)

# for the gap, it would have created separate IDs "27233947_1","27233947_2"
print(unique(hmm_data_fixed$ID[grepl("br23011", hmm_data_fixed$ID)]))
```

```{r}
bird_subset <- hmm_data_fixed %>% filter(grepl("br23011", ID))
p1 <- ggplot(data = bird_subset, aes(x = x, y = y, color = ID, group = ID)) +

print(p1)
```

```{r}
library(momentuHMM)
min_points <- 10 

# Filter out any ID groups that don't meet the threshold
hmm_data_filtered <- hmm_data_fixed %>%
  group_by(ID) %>%
  filter(n() >= min_points) %>%
  ungroup()

#crawlWrap to regularize GPS track to equal interval.
crw_out <- crawlWrap(obsData = hmm_data_filtered, 
                     timeStep = "1 hour", 
                     attempts = 70) #force the model to try multiple starting values if it gets stuck. resistant to crashing.

# prepData automatically calculates the metrics you need for HMM
model_ready_data <- prepData(data = crw_out)
#write.csv(model_ready_data, "/Users/yjkang/Desktop/HMM_Ready_eastMongolia_Crane.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#Convert UTM coordinates into continuous spatial lines per bird
crane_lines <- model_ready_data %>%
  filter(grepl("br22063", ID)) %>% #br23018 #br22064
  # Sort chronologically to ensure the line doesn't zigzag backward
  arrange(ID, time) %>% 
  # Tell R these are UTM Zone 49N meters (EPSG 32649)
  st_as_sf(coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32649) %>%
  # Transform back to Longitude/Latitude (EPSG 4326) for the map axes
  st_transform(crs = 4326) %>%
  # Group by individual bird and connect their dots into a single line
  group_by(ID) %>%
  summarize(do_union = FALSE) %>%
  st_cast("MULTIPOINT") #POINT #LINESTRING
```

```{r}
library(rnaturalearth)

basemap <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")
bbox <- st_bbox(crane_lines) # Calculate the bounding box of data, figures out the exact zoom level needed

# 5. Build the static map
static_map <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = basemap, fill = "gray95", color = "gray70") +
  geom_sf(data = crane_lines, aes(color = as.factor(ID)), size=0.05, alpha = 0.3) + #linewidth = 0.8
  
  # Zoom exactly to your data, adding a 2-degree padding margin so lines don't hit the edge
  coord_sf(xlim = c(bbox["xmin"] - 2, bbox["xmax"] + 2),
           ylim = c(bbox["ymin"] - 2, bbox["ymax"] + 2),
           expand = FALSE) +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_color_viridis_d(option = "turbo") +
  labs(title = "Regularized Migratory Trajectories",
      x = "Longitude",
      y = "Latitude") +
  theme(legend.position = "none", 
        panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray90", linetype = "dashed"),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14))
print(static_map)
#ggsave("/Users/yjkang/Desktop/Crane_Trajectory_Map.png", plot = static_map, width = 8, height = 8, dpi = 500)
```

=======================
HMM behaviour modeling
=======================
```{r, fig.height=3, fig.width=4}
crane_subset <- model_ready_data #%>% filter(grepl("br22064", ID))
raw_crane <- crane_subset %>% select(ID, time, x, y)
raw_crane$time <- as.POSIXct(raw_crane$time, tz = "UTC")
crane_data <- prepData(raw_crane)
crane_data$step <- crane_data$step / 1000 #convert to kilometers
crane_data$step[crane_data$step == 0] <- 0.0001 #GPS jitter can cause 0. We shift it by 1 meter. (step=Gamma distrib=always positive)

# Find where the step length is mathematically identical (the crawl straight lines)
is_interpolated <- c(FALSE, abs(diff(crane_data$step)) < 1e-5)
crane_data$step[is_interpolated] <- NA # Set the fake mathematical steps to NA
crane_data$angle[is_interpolated] <- NA
cat("\nNeutralized", sum(is_interpolated, na.rm = TRUE), "straight-line artifacts.\n")

hist(log(crane_data$step), breaks = 100)
hist(crane_data$angle, breaks = 100)
print(sum(crane_data$step == 0, na.rm = TRUE))
```

# ==========================================
# The 3-State Model (Migrating, Foraging, Roosting)
# ==========================================
```{r}
#Distribution type
#step=Gamma distrib, angle=Von Mises distrib
dist <- list(step = "gamma", angle = "vm")

#Parameters 
stepPar0_3  <- c(
  45.0, 2.0, 0.02,   # Means: Migration (45km), Foraging (2km), Roosting (20m)
  10.0, 1.5, 0.01 )  # SDs
anglePar0_3 <- c(
  8.0, 0.5, 0.1 )   # Concentrations: Migration 5.0 (highly directional), Foraging 0.5 (zigzagging), Roosting 0.1 (random/flat)
Par0_3 <- list(step = stepPar0_3, angle = anglePar0_3)

m3 <- fitHMM(#nlmPar = list(print.level = 2),
             data = crane_data, nbStates = 3, dist = dist, Par0 = Par0_3)
```

# ==========================================
# DECODING BEHAVIOR (The Viterbi Algorithm)
# ==========================================
```{r}
# Viterbi algorithm to assign State 1, 2, or 3 to every single row.
crane_data$Behavior_State <- viterbi(m3)
crane_data$Behavior_Name <- factor(crane_data$Behavior_State, 
                                   levels = c(1, 2, 3), 
                                   labels = c("Migrating", "Foraging", "Roosting"))
print(table(crane_data$Behavior_Name))
#write.csv(crane_data, "/Users/yjkang/Desktop/HMMoutput_Crane_Behavior.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Plot Gamma and Von Mises distributions
plot(m3, plotTracks = FALSE, ask = FALSE)
```

crane_angles <- subset(crane_data, !is.na(angle) & !is.na(Behavior_Name))

  geom_histogram(bins = 80, color = NA, alpha = 0.8, linewidth = 0.1) +

        strip.text = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
        panel.spacing = unit(2, "lines"),
        panel.grid = element_line(color = "grey75", linewidth = 0.3),
        axis.text.y = element_blank(), # Hide the confusing grid numbers
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank())
